surface_form_payload.question_text: Assign the frequency, severity, and qualitative risk categories independently.

parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: Design intent: V-001 receives well flow and discharges through its outlet lines within design throughput (CASE-01, CASE-03). The Flow/More deviation (CASE-02, CASE-03) has two credible, operationally initiated causes: gas-lift compressor commissioning and full opening of the well flow valves (CASE-04). These are intermittent planned or operator actions. They are plausible during the operating life, but there is no evidence of recurrence, which supports frequency C (Casual). No consequences are listed (CASE-05). Generically, excess throughput to a separator can cause level or pressure excursions, carryover into outlet lines, or elevated line velocities. Escalation to loss of containment or major damage is not evidenced, so severity III (Average) is assigned as a provisional mid-range rating. No safeguards are listed or credited (CASE-06). Matrix result: III x C = M. Recommendations: (1) define the consequences. (2) Verify separator, outlet-line and relief capacity against the maximum combined well and gas-lift flow. (3) Confirm level and pressure protection on V-001. (4) Require staged, controlled procedures for compressor commissioning and well valve opening. (5) Re-rank once consequences and safeguards are documented.
safeguards_considered: Existing safeguards: none are listed in the packet (CASE-06), and none are credited in the ranking.
Recommended for verification, not credited: check separator, outlet-line and pressure-relief capacity against the maximum combined well and gas-lift flow.
Recommended for verification, not credited: V-001 level and pressure control, with high-level and high-pressure alarms and independent trips.
Recommended administrative control, not credited: a staged, rate-limited procedure for gas-lift compressor commissioning and well flow valve opening, with separator conditions monitored.

supporting_evidence.relevance: Defines the node (separator V-001 and associated lines), which sets the design intent of handling well flow within vessel and outlet-line capacity.
Establishes the parameter and guideword pair under assessment: Flow/More.
Specifies the deviation scope: more flow in the separator vessel and its outlet lines.
Lists two credible, operationally initiated causes (gas-lift compressor commissioning, full opening of well flow valves). These support an occasional (C) likelihood rather than remote or frequent.
Lists no consequences, which drives the provisional mid-range severity and the reduced confidence.
Lists no safeguards, so no mitigation is credited and safeguard verification is recommended.

uncertainty_notes: CASE-05 lists no consequences, so severity III is a provisional mid-range placement rather than an evidence-derived rating. It could be II if the excess flow causes only a controllable operating upset. It could be IV if the combined well and gas-lift flow can exceed separator, outlet-line or relief capacity.
CASE-06 lists no safeguards. It is unknown whether safeguards are absent or simply undocumented, so no risk reduction is credited.
The packet gives no design capacities, well deliverability, gas-lift rates, operating history or frequency data. The frequency category is therefore purely judgmental.
Hydrocarbon well-fluid service is inferred from the cause descriptions (well flow valves, gas-lift compressor). The packet does not state it explicitly.
The M classification is fairly robust. Seven of the nine neighbouring matrix cells (severity II-IV x frequency B-D) also give M; only II-B gives L and only IV-D gives H.

Subjective probability is a judgment aid only; it is not derived from data and is not part of the qualitative matrix. It is defined as the chance that a consequential more-flow upset of V-001 from the listed causes occurs at least once over the facility operating life, estimated at about 30%.

You are an independent process-safety specialist conducting a single-pass HAZOP judgment for a controlled research experiment.

Use only the information supplied in the case packet. Do not invent plant facts, operating data, safeguards, incident histories, or causal evidence. Where the packet is insufficient, state the uncertainty explicitly. Apply the HAZOP logic of design intent, guideword/deviation, cause, consequence, safeguard, qualitative risk classification, and recommendation.

The risk matrix is qualitative and is intended for prioritization rather than quantitative risk calculation. Provide a concise evidence-oriented technical rationale; do not provide private chain-of-thought or a step-by-step hidden reasoning transcript. Return exactly one response conforming to the required structured-output schema, with no text outside that structure.
